properties.property: KZG commitment input MUST be exactly 48 bytes before versioned hash conversion
properties.rationale: Incorrect commitment length would produce invalid versioned hashes that don't match blob data

properties.property: Versioned hash output MUST be exactly 32 bytes with version byte 0x01 as first byte
properties.formal_specification: FORALL result: versioned_hash_ready(result) => len(result) == 32 AND result[0] == 0x01
properties.rationale: Versioned hash format must match EIP-4844 specification for blob transaction validation

properties.property: Versioned hash MUST be deterministically computed from commitment - same commitment always produces same hash
properties.formal_specification: FORALL c1, c2: c1 == c2 => versioned_hash(c1) == versioned_hash(c2)
properties.rationale: Non-deterministic hashing would break blob validation consensus across nodes

properties.property: All external byte inputs for G1 point validation MUST be treated as untrusted
properties.rationale: External inputs could be crafted to exploit validation logic or cause DoS

properties.property: G1 point at infinity MUST be accepted as valid without BLS verification
properties.formal_specification: FORALL input: input == G1_INFINITY_ENCODING => validate_g1(input) == VALID
properties.rationale: Point at infinity (0xc0 + 47 zero bytes) is a valid special case in BLS12-381

properties.property: G1 point validation MUST NOT accept points not on the BLS12-381 curve
properties.rationale: Off-curve points could be used to forge proofs or break pairing security

properties.property: BLS field element conversion MUST verify input is less than BLS modulus
properties.rationale: Values >= modulus are invalid field elements and could cause arithmetic errors

properties.property: Field element validation failure MUST raise an assertion error and halt operation
properties.formal_specification: FORALL input: int(input) >= BLS_MODULUS => bytes_to_bls_field(input) RAISES AssertionError
properties.rationale: Silent failure on invalid field elements could lead to cryptographic vulnerabilities

properties.property: All proof verification inputs MUST pass length validation before cryptographic operations
properties.formal_specification: FORALL proof_inputs: verify_proof(proof_inputs) => len(commitment) == 48 AND len(z) == 32 AND len(y) == 32 AND len(proof) == 48
properties.rationale: Incorrect input lengths could cause buffer overflows or invalid cryptographic operations

properties.property: KZG proof verification MUST use trusted setup parameter KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 for X - z computation
properties.rationale: Using incorrect trusted setup would produce wrong verification results

properties.property: Pairing check failure MUST result in proof rejection - no fallback acceptance
properties.formal_specification: FORALL pairing_result: pairing_result != FQ12.one() => proof_valid == FALSE
properties.rationale: Accepting failed pairing checks would allow invalid blob data to be included in blocks

properties.property: Valid KZG proof MUST cryptographically attest that y = P(z) for polynomial P committed in commitment
properties.formal_specification: FORALL valid_proof: proof_valid(commitment, z, y, proof) => polynomial_eval(commitment, z) == y
properties.rationale: This is the core security property of KZG - proof of polynomial evaluation correctness

properties.property: Trusted setup compromise MUST be detected or the entire KZG system is insecure
properties.formal_specification: ASSUMPTION: KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 generated via secure multi-party computation with at least one honest participant
properties.rationale: Compromised trusted setup would allow forging valid proofs for arbitrary data - complete security failure

properties.property: ethereum_blockchain_height gauge MUST be updated atomically when new block is processed
properties.rationale: Stale or inconsistent height metrics would provide incorrect sync status to monitoring

properties.property: ethereum_best_known_block_number MUST be >= ethereum_blockchain_height
properties.rationale: Best known block should never be lower than processed height - indicates sync regression

properties.property: ethereum_peer_count MUST accurately reflect current number of connected peers
properties.formal_specification: FORALL peer_event: (connect OR disconnect)(peer_event) => eventually(ethereum_peer_count == actual_peer_count)
properties.rationale: Incorrect peer count could mask network isolation attacks from monitoring

properties.property: Metrics endpoint MUST NOT expose sensitive operational data to unauthenticated requesters
properties.rationale: Attackers could use metrics for timing attacks or operational intelligence gathering

properties.property: Metrics response MUST conform to Prometheus exposition format
properties.rationale: Invalid format would break Prometheus scraping and monitoring dashboards

properties.property: Metrics using ethereum_ prefix MUST match EIP-2159 standard definitions
properties.formal_specification: FORALL metric: metric.name.startswith('ethereum_') => metric IN EIP2159_STANDARD_METRICS
properties.rationale: Non-standard metrics with ethereum_ prefix cause cross-client monitoring inconsistencies

properties.property: Client-specific metrics MUST NOT use ethereum_ prefix
properties.rationale: Prevents namespace pollution and metric conflicts across client implementations

properties.property: Absent fields in ProgressiveContainer MUST consume zero bytes in serialized output
properties.rationale: Core benefit of progressive containers - compact serialization with optional fields

properties.property: Deserialization MUST initialize absent fields to their type's default (zero) value
properties.rationale: Ensures consistent state regardless of which fields were present in serialized form

properties.property: Deserialization MUST validate serialized bytes against active_fields before reconstruction
properties.formal_specification: FORALL bytes: deserialize(bytes) => validate_against_active_fields(bytes, active_fields) == TRUE
properties.rationale: Untrusted serialized data could exploit deserialization logic without validation

properties.property: Field positions in Merkle tree MUST remain stable based on active_fields bit positions
properties.formal_specification: FORALL field, version1, version2: gindex(field, version1) == gindex(field, version2) IF field IN both_versions
properties.rationale: Stable gindices enable light client proofs to work across schema versions

properties.property: Final hash_tree_root MUST include active_fields mix-in to prevent collision attacks
properties.rationale: Without mix-in, absent fields would hash identically to zero-valued fields - security vulnerability

properties.property: Containers with different active_fields MUST produce different hash_tree_roots even if field values are identical
properties.formal_specification: FORALL c1, c2: c1.active_fields != c2.active_fields => hash_tree_root(c1) != hash_tree_root(c2)
properties.rationale: Prevents attackers from forging proofs by manipulating which fields appear present

properties.property: Progressive container MUST have at least one field
properties.rationale: Empty containers have no meaningful serialization or merkleization

properties.property: Progressive container MUST NOT exceed 256 active fields
properties.rationale: 256-bit bitvector limit is a hard protocol constraint

properties.property: active_fields bitvector MUST NOT have trailing zero bits
properties.rationale: Trailing zeros would create ambiguity in container schema interpretation

properties.property: Number of 1 bits in active_fields MUST equal number of actual fields in container
properties.rationale: Mismatch would indicate corrupted schema or malicious container definition

properties.property: Merkle proofs from untrusted sources MUST be fully validated before accepting field values
properties.rationale: Accepting unverified proofs would allow attackers to inject false field values

properties.property: Merkle proof verification MUST compute expected gindex based on active_fields positions
properties.formal_specification: FORALL proof, field: verify_proof(proof, field) => expected_gindex == compute_gindex(active_fields, field)
properties.rationale: Incorrect gindex computation would allow proof forgery for different fields

properties.property: Proof verification MUST validate active_fields mix-in to prevent absent/zero field collision
properties.formal_specification: FORALL proof: verify_proof(proof) => verify_active_fields_mixin(proof.root, active_fields) == TRUE
properties.rationale: Without mix-in verification, proofs for absent fields could be forged using zero values

properties.property: Valid Merkle proof MUST cryptographically bind field value to container hash_tree_root
properties.formal_specification: FORALL valid_proof: proof_valid(proof, value, root) => value authentically belongs to container with hash_tree_root == root
properties.rationale: Core security property - proofs attest to authentic field membership

properties.property: Light clients MUST have access to correct container schema to verify proofs
properties.rationale: Outdated schemas would cause valid proofs to be rejected or invalid proofs to be accepted

properties.property: SHA256 hash function MUST remain collision-resistant for Merkle security
properties.formal_specification: ASSUMPTION: !exists(m1, m2): m1 != m2 AND sha256(m1) == sha256(m2)
properties.rationale: Hash collisions would allow forging Merkle proofs for arbitrary field values
